Definition: to store away, i.e. (figuratively) in the memory
BiblicalUsage: Kamac means to store away — to lay up in the memory, to keep in reserve. Moses says of God's judgment, is not this laid up in store with me, and sealed up among my treasures?
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that God forgets nothing: vengeance is stored up with Him, sealed among His treasures, and the day of reckoning comes in His time, not mine.
